3R replication script (analysis.R)

How to replicate: save the block below as analysis.R, place cleaned.csv (in the export bundle) beside it, then run Rscript analysis.R. The script prints every table shown in the app; the app's numbers were verified byte-for-byte against native R output. Package citations are in section 6.
# Reproducible analysis script generated by Telos
# Run from the folder holding cleaned.csv. Uncomment install.packages() the first time.
# install.packages(c("modelsummary", "effectsize", "emmeans", "ggplot2"))
library(modelsummary)
library(effectsize)
library(emmeans)
library(ggplot2)
d <- read.csv("cleaned.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d[["teaching_method"]] <- factor(d[["teaching_method"]])

# === 01 · One-way ANOVA + post-hoc ===
owa <- data.frame(y = d[["exam_score"]], g = factor(d[["teaching_method"]]))
print(datasummary_balance(~g, data = owa, dinm = FALSE))  # Table 1 (Arel-Bundock datasummary)
m <- aov(d[["exam_score"]] ~ factor(d[["teaching_method"]]), data = owa)
print(summary(m))
print(effectsize::eta_squared(m, partial = FALSE))
m2 <- aov(y ~ g, data = owa)  # named-factor refit so emmeans can reference the grouping term
print(summary(pairs(emmeans::emmeans(m2, ~ g), adjust = "tukey"), infer = TRUE, level = 0.99))
gf <- factor(d[["teaching_method"]]); agg <- data.frame(g = levels(gf), m = as.numeric(tapply(d[["exam_score"]], gf, mean)))
nn <- as.numeric(tapply(d[["exam_score"]], gf, length)); sdv <- as.numeric(tapply(d[["exam_score"]], gf, sd))
se <- sdv / sqrt(nn); tq <- qt(1 - (1 - 0.99) / 2, nn - 1)
agg$lo <- agg$m - tq * se; agg$hi <- agg$m + tq * se
print(ggplot(agg, aes(g, m)) + geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), colour = "#0c447c") + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL))

The F and its p tell you whether the groups differ overall; $\eta$\textsuperscript{2} (or $\omega$\textsuperscript{2}) is the effect size. If significant, the post-hoc table shows which specific pairs differ, with multiplicity-adjusted p-values. Your significance threshold ($\alpha$) is 0.05.

A one-way ANOVA gave F(2,237)=43.07, p $<$ .001, $\eta$\textsuperscript{2}=.27 [.16, 1.00]. Tukey HSD post-hoc tests showed\ldots{}

Statistical basis: F-test for equality of several means (ANOVA) (Fisher, R. A. (1925). Statistical Methods for Research Workers. Oliver \& Boyd.); Tukey HSD post-hoc comparison (Tukey, J. W. (1949). "Comparing individual means in the analysis of variance." Biometrics, 5(2), 99-114.); Bonferroni-corrected post-hoc comparison (a 'posthoc' choice) (Dunn, O. J. (1961). "Multiple comparisons among means." Journal of the American Statistical Association, 56(293), 52-64.); Scheff\'{e}-corrected post-hoc comparison (a 'posthoc' choice) (Scheff\'{e}, H. (1953). "A method for judging all contrasts in the analysis of variance." Biometrika, 40(1-2), 87-104.); Levene's test for equal variances (Brown-Forsythe median-centered variant) (Levene, H. (1960). "Robust tests for equality of variances." In I. Olkin (Ed.), Contributions to Probability and Statistics (pp. 278-292). Stanford University Press.); Brown-Forsythe median-centered variant of the homogeneity-of-variance test (Brown, M. B., Forsythe, A. B. (1974). "Robust tests for the equality of variances." Journal of the American Statistical Association, 69(346), 364-367.); $\eta$\textsuperscript{2} effect-size benchmarks (Cohen, J. (1988). Statistical Power Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences (2nd ed.). Routledge.).

Harness README
# 07 · One-way ANOVA + post-hoc

**Question:** do 3+ groups differ, and which pairs?

**Scenario:** Campus study: which teaching method produces the highest exam scores (99% CI)?

## Input configuration

- **Dataset:** `campus-study.csv`
- **Configure-data:** app defaults (auto-detected types/levels)
- **Options:** post-hoc: Tukey HSD (explicit); CI: 99% (explicit)

**Role assignments** (drag column → slot):

| Column | Role slot |
|---|---|
| `exam_score` | outcome |
| `teaching_method` | factor |
